remarks_1999: Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, and Abiquiú Notebooks date 1923 and indicate included in 1924 New York (Anderson) exhibition as one of eight paintings (nos. 35–42) titled *Leaves*. Yet all three archives title the painting *Pattern of Leaves*, which was not among titles on the 1924 exhibition checklist. Stretcher inscription 1 dates the work to 1 May 1924 and Phillips Collection files include photocopy of original label on work that indicates, "'Autumn Leaf – Oak' 1924" [Alfred Stieglitz, label: printed, The Intimate Gallery, black ink]. These inscriptions, if correct in terms of date, indicate that work was painted rather than exhibited in 1924. Yet their validity is compromised by the inaccuracy of the label: printed, The Intimate Gallery title inscription: the work is of a maple, not an oak, leaf. The 1925 New York (Anderson) checklist includes three leaf paintings: no. 107, "Leaf Motive – No. I"; no. 108, "Leaf Motive – No. 2,"; and no. 109, "Leaf Motive – No. 3." In Abiquiú Notebooks and Downtown Gallery Archive, photographs accompany entries for "Leaf Motif – No. I" and "Leaf Motif – No. 2," but "Leaf Motif – No. 3" is not documented visually nor are its dimensions included in the entry. Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, and Abiquiú Notebooks indicate that 'Pattern of Leaves' was no. 109 in the 1925 exhibition and purchased by George Herbert Engelhard, Stieglitz's brother–in–law. Whitney Archive and Abiquiú Notebooks also indicate, "Note: April, 1946, O'Keeffe says belongs to Georgia Engelhard, stored at An American Place. May, 1946: On looking at pictures of #1 and #2 Leaf Motifs, O'Keeffe thinks one of them is Engelhards." Yet, both Whitney Archive and Abiquiú Notebooks explain that when O'Keeffe further considered the photographs of "Leaf Motif – No. I" and "Leaf Motif – No. 2," she became unsure as to which one Engelhard had purchased. In fact, Engelhard owned "Leaf Motif, No. I," see cat. no. 466. For Leaf Motif – No. 2," see cat. no. 467. Museum files indicate that Stieglitz sent Duncan Phillips a painting titled "Leaf Motif, No. 1" on 22 January 1926 for purchase consideration and that Phillips returned it to him on 17 March 1926, after having included it in a 1–28 February 1926 exhibition at the Phillips Collection that titled it "Leaf Motif, No. 1." They also document Phillip's having purchased a painting titled "Oak Leaf" on 15 March 1926. Phillips loaned this work to a 1927 BMA exhibition, where it was titled "Pattern of Leaves." He exhibited it at the Phillips Collection in November 1927 as "Leaf Pattern" and loaned it to a 1929 Atlanta exhibition, where it was reproduced in the catalogue and titled "Oak Leaves." It seems clear that Stieglitz wrote "Autumn Leaf – Oak" rather than "Autumn Leaf – Maple" on the label: printed, The Intimate Gallery label affixed to the backing of the work that Phillips purchased on 15 March 1926. Because neither O'Keeffe nor Irvine examined the work in 1946 [and did not realize that it dated from 1924], O'Keeffe mistakenly associated the work with the 1924 rather than the 1925 exhibition. Because neither the 1924 nor 1925 checklists include a painting titled "Patterns of Leaves," O'Keeffe must have provided Irvine with the title, probably because it had been published as such by Duncan Phillips in *A Collection in the Making* (1926), and thus, the title was transferred to Downtown Gallery Archive, and Abiquiú Notebooks. In any case, because O'Keeffe dated its stretcher 1924 and Stieglitz dated it 1924 on the label: printed, The Intimate Gallery label, both sometime before 1926, it was completed in 1924 and exhibited in the 1925 Anderson exhibition as "Leaf Motive – No. 3." Finally, the painting was purchased from Stieglitz two days before Phillips returned "Leaf Motif No. I" and, most conclusively, there are no leaf paintings dating before 1924 that have this work's characteristics. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.notes: Source of title: Duncan Phillips in 1926 and O'Keeffe in the mid-1940s, Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks.
titles.title: Pattern of Leaves

description: A burgundy leaf with a split running down it sits atop a pale, grayish white leaf. Behind these two, a darker gray leaf is barely visible. The three leaves fill the canvas, with only small bits of the plain, cream-colored background visible on the edges of the composition.
title: Pattern of Leaves
